clue.text: Game birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a children's party game played sitting in a circle
second meaning: two ducks and a goose, read as a list of fowl

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as pheasant and grouse; split it and 'Game' is a playground game while 'birds' is three of them, named in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game, where one player taps heads round a circle, is named after the waterfowl called out during play.

clue.text: Spinner's round pitch, backing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the order runs backwards

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
to lob is to pitch or toss upwards
backing is support or help

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's ball bounces on a round pitch and kicks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' and 'pitch' suggest cricket, but the spinner is a juggling toy. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabolo is a two-cup toy spun on a string held between two sticks, so it is literally a spinner.

clue.text: Eats cold cuts

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to hew is to cut with an axe or blade

explanation.surface: Someone has sliced meat from the fridge for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold cuts' looks like one phrase for sliced meats; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew is to grind food with the teeth, the main action of eating, so chews stands loosely for eats.

clue.text: Ta-da! All the information's here

parts.note: surface reading: a magician's flourish presenting a finished trick
setter's reading: these four letters are the word for facts rearranged, so the exclamation is that word put into a new setting

explanation.surface: Someone triumphantly unveils a complete file of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue within a clue: TA-DA is DATA with its letters set in a new order, and 'set' is a familiar anagram signal, so TA-DA is a DATA SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A dataset is a complete collection of related records, so it holds all the information on its subject.

clue.text: No matter what half of all comedies raised, normal show is next

indicators.note: only the front half of each of the following words is kept, the back half of every one being dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, a TV schedule of comedy repeats carries on as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word after 'half of all' loses its second half: COMEdies, RAIsed, NORmal, SHow, Is, NExt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means whatever the weather or circumstances, so it is a way of saying regardless of anything.

clue.text: On reflection, love story ending in wedding is sweet

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a tale is a story

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of wedding

explanation.surface: Looking back, a romance that ended in marriage was a sweet one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian ice cream, served as a dessert, which British English also calls a sweet.

clue.text: Men fine with one article by Blair?

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
fine and well both mean in good health
I is the Roman numeral one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a team of men and a newspaper piece written by Prime Minister Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blair is not Tony: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair, so something by Blair is Orwellian. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwellian means in the manner of George Orwell, the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair, so it describes his work.

clue.text: Academic reported on EastEnders for cover of Spectator

indicators.note: spoken in the accent of the London soap's Cockney characters, who drop their initial h sounds

parts.note: highbrow means academic or intellectual; without its first h it is said like the hairy ridge

explanation.surface: A scholar has written about the BBC soap EastEnders for the cover of The Spectator magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the h. The Spectator is a magazine, but here a spectator is anyone watching, and the eyebrow sits over the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is the strip of hair above an onlooker's eye, so it covers the organ a spectator watches with.

clue.text: Speed, beginning to pass point of no return

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the first letter of pass
in tennis an ace is a serve the receiver cannot return, winning the point

explanation.surface: A runner speeds past the moment after which they cannot turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of no return' is a stock phrase for an irreversible moment; here it is a tennis point won from an unreturnable serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Pace means rate of movement, so it is a synonym for speed as in walking at a fast pace.

clue.text: Roll joint, getting one blown away

parts.note: to tumble is to roll over and over
a joint is a cannabis cigarette, and weed is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone rolls a cannabis joint and ends up stoned out of their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown away' sounds like being amazed or stoned; it is literally a plant that the wind bowls along.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a dry plant that breaks from its root and is driven along the ground by the wind.

clue.text: I hate this way south for hikes

parts.note: what an audience shouts at something it dislikes
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A walker grumbles about a route heading south on a long hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hikes' looks like walks; it is the verb meaning raises, as in hikes prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to raise or increase, the same as to hike prices or rates.

clue.text: King Lear's mad, holding heartless test to reveal snakes

parts.note: R is for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within the other
something mad is deranged, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear goes mad on the heath, tested to the point of seeing serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Lear' wants to be read as one name, the Shakespeare tragedy; split it and King is the Latin Rex, while Lear's, with its S, is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattlers is an informal American name for rattlesnakes, named for the rattle on the tail.

clue.text: Bush changed history in foreign affairs, primarily

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means it goes inside it
something changed has been altered, so these letters take a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: the first letter of foreign
the letters of history rearranged
the first letter of affairs

explanation.surface: President George W. Bush changed the course of history through foreign affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the US president; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub that flowers bright yellow in early spring, so it is a kind of bush.

clue.text: Scrap Conservative implicated in crime — everyone's upset with it

indicators.note: to be implicated in something is to be caught up inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down entry the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: all means everyone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory politician caught up in a criminal scandal, and everyone is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside SIN; then ALL with IT is turned over to follow. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or particle, as in not a scintilla of evidence, so it is a scrap.

clue.text: Survey that is collected by car manufacturer

indicators.note: being collected by someone means being picked up and held, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: VW is Volkswagen, the German car maker
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A customer questionnaire picked up from a car dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey and to view both mean to look over or inspect, and as nouns both mean a broad look.

clue.text: Source of fake news about protest

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: someone who tells untruths is where false stories come from

explanation.surface: A disinformation outlet putting out stories about a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of fake news' tempts a solver to take the first letter of fake; the whole phrase is a person who invents stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain or protest bitterly, as in rail against injustice.

clue.text: Shed drove me nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their garden shed is driving them crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut; it is the past tense of the verb, as in shed a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed as a past verb means took off or got rid of, as a snake sheds its skin, so it equals removed.

clue.text: 100 daguerreotypes? They're cool

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
daguerreotypes are early photographs, so they are old snaps

explanation.surface: A collection of a hundred antique photos that collectors find very cool.
explanation.walkthrough: A daguerreotype is a nineteenth-century photograph on a silvered plate; 'cool' looks like praise but means chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold snaps are short spells of chilly weather, so they are periods that are cool.

clue.text: Democrat's launched opposition

parts.note: D for Democrat, with the 's read as is
to launch something is to send it off

explanation.surface: A Democrat has launched an attack on the opposing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement with an official view, so it is a form of opposition.

clue.text: Design colour that's largely relabelled?

indicators.note: putting a new label on something swaps one tag for another, so one size marking is replaced

parts.note: purple is a colour
L is the clothing size large
OS is the clothing size outsize, the bigger tag put on in its place

explanation.surface: A designer asks whether a colour has been mostly renamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like mostly; read as large-ly it is L, the size tag, which is swapped for OS (outsize) in PURPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Design can mean intention, as in by design, so it is a synonym for purpose.

clue.text: One rubbing husband, a halfwit, up the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way up a down entry means reading from the bottom, so the order is backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
a fool is a halfwit

explanation.surface: Someone is rubbing their dim husband up the wrong way, irritating him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halfwit' tempts a solver to take half of wit; it is simply a dim person.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge for scrubbing, so it is something rubbing the skin.

clue.text: Time soon mends feelings

indicators.note: mending something puts it back together, so these letters are reassembled in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Time will soon heal hurt feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the proverb that time heals, with 'mends' doing the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions and feelings are synonyms for states such as joy, anger or sorrow.

clue.text: More than one way to prepare a tomato

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to dry in the sun, as Italian tomatoes are

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a recipe saying there are several ways to prepare a tomato; it splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry is an adjective meaning various or miscellaneous, and to sun-dry is to preserve food by drying it in sunlight.

clue.text: Stocking filler for horny loners

indicators.note: the filling of something is its inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: inside these words

explanation.surface: A cheeky Christmas stocking present for lonely, randy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking filler' reads as one phrase for a small gift; split it and Stocking is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made of the synthetic fibre, so a single nylon is a stocking.

clue.text: Old gangster turned into evil political icon

indicators.note: put into something means placed inside it, so pieces go within another word

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
the first part of VICE, evil-doing
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
O is the abbreviation for old
the rest of VICE, wickedness

explanation.surface: A one-time mobster has become a wicked figurehead in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like a reversal or anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym: milk that has turned has gone sour. Evil is VICE, which opens up to take the gangster and that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval Office is the US president's room in the White House and a symbol of the presidency, so a political icon.

clue.text: John Travolta's beginning to get sack

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its first letter, so just that one is used

parts.note: the first letter of Travolta

explanation.surface: The actor John Travolta's early career nearly got him fired.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like Travolta's first name; it is the slang word for a toilet. Loo is the British word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, and to loot is to steal goods by force, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Penalty in back of the net has decent shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are knocked into a new order
the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football penalty kick hits the back of the net with a decent strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of the net' is football's phrase for a goal; here only 'back of' signals, taking one letter from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A death sentence is the severest punishment a court can pass, so it is a penalty.
